topic: Lawrence Weiskrantz (1974): 'Blindsight' — Patient D.B. Pointing With 90% Accuracy Into Total Conscious Darkness
visual_mode_reason: Lawrence Weiskrantz and Elizabeth Warrington's 1974 discovery of 'Blindsight' in Patient D.B. — clinically blind in his left visual field after right V1 removal yet pointing to lights and guessing X-vs-O at >90% accuracy — directly maps the two visual pathways (conscious V1 cortex vs unconscious superior colliculus / pulvinar subcortical bypass).

primary_case.title: Lawrence Weiskrantz, Elizabeth Warrington, M. D. Sanders & J. Marshall's 1974 Patient D.B. 'Blindsight' discovery
primary_case.place: National Hospital for Nervous Diseases, Queen Square, London & University of Oxford

people.name: Lawrence Weiskrantz
people.role: Oxford experimental psychologist who coined the word 'Blindsight' in 1974 after persuading clinically blind Patient D.B. to 'just guess' into his dark visual field

people.name: Patient 'D.B.'
people.role: Young British man whose right primary visual cortex (V1 / calcarine cortex) was surgically removed at Queen Square to cure a benign vascular malformation triggering severe migraines — leaving his left visual field consciously pitch-dark

people.name: Elizabeth K. Warrington & Nicholas Humphrey
people.role: Queen Square neuropsychologist co-discoverer and Cambridge primate researcher whose monkey 'Helen' inspired Weiskrantz to test human hand-pointing inside blind fields

core_facts.fact: Standard neurology before 1974 taught a simple rule: destroy human primary visual cortex (**V1** at the back of the occipital lobe), and the opposite half of space goes permanently, 100% blind — because physicians only ever asked *'Tell me when you SEE the light'*.

Inspired by Nicholas Humphrey's monkey 'Helen' (who caught moving currants without V1), Elizabeth Warrington and Lawrence Weiskrantz tested **Patient D.B.** at Queen Square in 1973-1974 after surgical removal of his right V1 left his left visual field completely blind on standard hospital perimetry.

Instead of asking 'Do you see anything?' (to which D.B. always truthfully answered **'Nothing at all — zero!'**), Weiskrantz changed the rules to **forced-choice guessing**: *'Reach out and touch where a target MIGHT be'* or *'Just guess like flipping a coin: was it an X or an O, horizontal or vertical lines?'*

D.B. laughed that guessing in total blackness was ridiculous — yet across dozens of trials his finger landed **almost dead-center on silent light spots across 30 degrees of his 'blind' field**, and he discriminated **X vs O and line orientations at 85% to >95% accuracy** while insisting he saw NOTHING.
When Weiskrantz finally showed D.B. his own scorecard in *Brain* / *The Lancet* (1974), D.B. was utterly dumbstruck: *'Did I really do that?. I didn't see a thing — it was pure guesswork!'*

Careful controls ruled out stray light bouncing onto D.B.'s good half-retina (flashing targets onto the natural optic-disc blind spot inside the blind field dropped accuracy right down to 50% chance!).

How did D.B.'s hand know what 'he' didn't see? About 10% of optic-nerve fibers bypass V1 completely, branching down to the ancient midbrain **superior colliculus**, **pulvinar**, and lateral geniculate shortcuts straight into dorsal action/motion areas (MT/V5) — guiding eyes and hands WITHOUT switching on conscious awareness.

Decades later, Beatrice de Gelder and Marco Tamietto discovered **'Affective Blindsight'** in bilateral-V1-stroke patient **T.N.**: completely cortically blind across BOTH eyes, T.N. walked down a long corridor weaving cleanly around chairs, boxes, and tripods without a single collision — AND unconsciously flinched/smiled in facial EMG when shown unseen fearful vs happy faces via the superior-colliculus to amygdala shortcut.

In Weiskrantz et al.'s (1974) forced-choice reaching and grating orientation trials, Patient D.B. reported zero conscious sight in his scotoma yet exceeded 90% accuracy — reaching roughly 93% on spatial localization blocks.

wow_facts.fact: Ask Patient D.B. what he sees on his left and he swears on his life: **'Pitch black — nothing!'** Tell him 'Just point anyway,' and his finger lands dead on the silent target 9 times out of 10 — leaving D.B. gasping when shown his own chart.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Seeing and consciously KNOWING you see are two separate systems in the human brain.

wow_facts.fact: In 2008, a doctor with strokes in BOTH visual cortices (Patient T.N.) — clinically blind across his entire visual world — put down his white cane and zig-zagged cleanly around trash cans, chairs, and boxes down a hospital hallway without touching a single obstacle.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Your ancient midbrain obstacle radar works even when conscious sight is dark.

wow_facts.fact: Show an angry or terrified face inside a blindsight field: the patient swears nobody was on the display, yet their amygdala lights up and their own cheek/brow muscles unconsciously mirror the emotion.
wow_facts.why_surprising: 'Affective Blindsight': catching human emotion without conscious sight.

wow_facts.fact: For a hundred years doctors missed Blindsight simply because they asked *'Raise your hand IF you see it'* instead of *'Guess left or right even when you see nothing'*.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Changing one question unlocked the neuroscience of consciousness.

misconceptions.myth: Patients with Blindsight are secretly peeking or seeing blurry dim shadows.
misconceptions.truth: In 'Type 1 Blindsight', subjective visibility is genuinely zero even on high-confidence betting scales — which is why blindsight patients can starve in front of a glass of water on their blind side unless explicitly prompted by someone else to 'guess'.

misconceptions.myth: Unconscious blindsight proves conscious awareness is a useless decoration ('epiphenomenon').
misconceptions.truth: Just the opposite. Without conscious V1 sight, Patient D.B. NEVER spontaneously reached for a cup or initiated plans toward objects in his blind field — consciousness is what lets you act *on your own* without an experimenter prompting 'guess now!'

misconceptions.myth: Only humans have two visual streams.
misconceptions.truth: Evolution built the ancient midbrain collicular 'Where is it moving?' radar in fish, frogs, and mammals hundreds of millions of years before expanding primate V1 high-definition conscious cortex.

everyday_hooks: Ducking or jerking your hand back from a flying ball in peripheral vision half a second BEFORE your conscious mind registers what the object even was.
Walking down stairs reading something else and catching a misstep automatically via dorsal/subcortical action vision.
Realizing why 'having a gut hunch' sometimes reflects real sub-threshold sensory processing.
